summary.name: KeyStats
summary.one_liner: A menu bar / system tray app that tracks aggregate keyboard and mouse activity (key presses, clicks, movement, scrolling) without recording typed text, with optional end-to-end encrypted multi-device sync.
keywords: how many keys i press per day
use_cases: see how many clicks and mouse movement per day
view keyboard heatmap over a date range
find which apps get the most key presses
sync key statistics across multiple Macs with encryption
summary.what_it_does: KeyStats runs in the menu bar or system tray and shows daily key presses, mouse clicks, pointer movement, and scroll distance. It offers trends, recent history, long-term totals, and per-key and key-combination counts, plus a keyboard heatmap across a date range. Per-app breakdowns show which apps account for key presses, clicks, and scrolling, using only aggregate counts. Optional pairing syncs supported daily key and mouse-button statistics encrypted on-device, and the current device's statistics can be exported and imported as JSON.
notable: Records only aggregate counts: no typed text, key sequences, or cursor/click coordinates
Local storage by default; sync is opt-in and encrypted on-device before upload
Open source, installable via Homebrew on macOS 13 or later
JSON export and import of device statistics
caveats: Mouse movement, scroll distance, and per-app statistics are not currently synced
Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later for the Homebrew install
Linux support is only a community build from a different repository (0x5c0f/keyStats)
Requires granting a system permission to monitor input
